title: Investigation of Berberine's Cardioprotective Effects and Its Association With the Notch Signaling Pathway in Rat Myocardial Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury.
authors: Jiang, Daxing; Tang, Xin; Yang, Haifan; Cheng, Hong
one_liner_zh: 该文研究小檗碱在大鼠心肌缺血再灌注损伤中的保护作用及Notch信号通路，虽含分子对接但对象为小分子-蛋白，非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Ischemia-reperfusion injury poses a significant challenge in cardiac pathology, leading to myocardial cell damage and dysfunction. Berberine, a natural compound, has shown potential cardioprotective effects. This study aims to investigate the protective role of berberine in myocardial cells post-ischemia-reperfusion injury, focusing on its modulation of the Neurogenic locus notch homolog protein (Notch) signaling pathway. METHODS: Male rats were subjected to ischemia-reperfusion injury and treated with berberine. Triphenyltetrazolium chloride (TTC) and hematoxylin and eosin (HE) staining were used to assess myocardial tissue damage and structure. Gene expression of Neurogenic locus notch homolog protein 1 (Notch1), Hairy and enhancer of split-1 (Hes1), B-cell lymphoma 2 (Bcl-2), and Bcl-2-associated X protein (Bax) was analyzed using Quantitative Polymerase Chain Reaction (qPCR). Apoptosis rate in myocardial cells was evaluated using Terminal deoxynucleotidyl Transferase dUTP Nick End Labeling (TUNEL) staining. Protein expression of Bcl-2 and Bax was examined. Molecular docking and Microscale Thermophoresis (MST) validation were performed to investigate the interaction between berberine and Notch1. RESULTS: Berberine treatment was associated with effective protection of myocardial tissue post-ischemia-reperfusion, indicated by reduced infarct area (p < 0.05) and improvements in tissue structure. Coinciding with these observations, berberine also influenced the expression of Notch1, Hes1, Bcl-2, and Bax in myocardial tissue, alongside modulation of Bcl-2 and Bax protein levels (p < 0.05). Additionally, molecular studies revealed that berberine binds to Notch1, suggesting a potential interaction. CONCLUSION: The study suggests an association between berberine's cardioprotective effects and Notch signaling pathway modulation in the context of myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury. While berberine was found to bind Notch1 and affect gene and protein expression related to apoptosis, further research is necessary to determine whether these effects directly contribute to reduced apoptosis and enhanced cell survival.
abstract_zh: 背景：缺血再灌注损伤是心脏病理学中的一个重大挑战，导致心肌细胞损伤和功能障碍。小檗碱（berberine）作为一种天然化合物，已显示出潜在的心脏保护作用。本研究旨在探讨小檗碱在缺血再灌注损伤后心肌细胞中的保护作用，重点关注其对神经源性位点缺口同源蛋白（Notch）信号通路的调节。方法：雄性大鼠接受缺血再灌注损伤并用小檗碱处理。使用三苯基四氮唑氯化物（TTC）和苏木精-伊红（HE）染色评估心肌组织损伤和结构。通过定量聚合酶链反应（qPCR）分析神经源性位点缺口同源蛋白1（Notch1）、发状分裂增强子-1（Hes1）、B细胞淋巴瘤2（Bcl-2）和Bcl-2相关X蛋白（Bax）的基因表达。使用末端脱氧核苷酸转移酶dUTP缺口末端标记（TUNEL）染色评估心肌细胞凋亡率。检测Bcl-2和Bax的蛋白表达。进行分子对接和微量热泳动（MST）验证以研究小檗碱与Notch1之间的相互作用。结果：小檗碱处理与缺血再灌注后心肌组织的有效保护相关，表现为梗死面积减少（p < 0.05）和组织结构改善。与这些观察一致，小檗碱还影响心肌组织中Notch1、Hes1、Bcl-2和Bax的表达，同时调节Bcl-2和Bax蛋白水平（p < 0.05）。此外，分子研究表明小檗碱与Notch1结合，提示潜在相互作用。结论：本研究提示，在心肌缺血再灌注损伤背景下，小檗碱的心脏保护作用与Notch信号通路调节之间存在关联。虽然发现小檗碱能结合Notch1并影响与凋亡相关的基因和蛋白表达，但需要进一步研究以确定这些效应是否直接促进凋亡减少和细胞存活增强。
